     A design brainstorm, not a spec. Captured per CLAUDE.md so the analysis survives a context reset. -->

# Working Groups page and zero-maintenance cost.eu sync — design

## 1. Executive summary

We add one dedicated `/working-groups.html` page (Option A: a single document with four anchored sections `#wg1`–`#wg4`) and convert every leadership and membership surface on the site from hand-coded HTML to render-from-JSON, so that a change on cost.eu reaches the home page, the About page, the directory, and the new page through a single weekly data sync with no hand-edits. The headline is a new `data/wg.json` written by `scripts/sync-cost.py` plus a structured `wg_leadership` field finally populated in `data/bios.json`. Today's audit and the live tree confirm both are written empty and only hand-seeded, so the load-bearing build step is teaching `sync-cost.py` to derive them. The only content that cannot be synced (cost.eu does not expose WG titles or purposes) is four short hand-authored, hand-translated descriptions, owned in one place and carried forward untouched by every sync. The 3 to 4 day cost.eu publishing lag is surfaced honestly with a quiet "synced from cost.eu, updated `<date>`" cue rather than pretended away.

## 2. The Working Groups page (Option A)

### 2.1 Page shape

One `<main id="main">` carrying a single `<h1>`, an intro with the sync cue, a jump nav that doubles as a table of contents, and four `<section id="wg{1..4}">` blocks. Heading order is `h1` (page) then `h2` (per WG) then `h3` (Leadership / Members / Activities). The page follows the established render-from-JSON contract from `assets/js/home-events.js`: a single fetch, `pickLocale(obj, locale, fallback)`, an off-DOM `DocumentFragment`, fail-soft to the static HTML already in the markup, and `container.dataset.renderedFromJson = '1'` on success.

```html
<main id="main">
  <section class="wg-page-head">
    <div class="container reveal">
      <span class="eyebrow">Structure</span>
      <h1>Working Groups</h1>
      <p class="lede">The Action pursues its three objectives through four interconnected Working Groups.</p>
      <p class="wg-synced glass" data-sync-cue>
        Membership and leadership shown here follow the COST directory.
        <span class="wg-synced-stamp">Updated <time datetime=""></time></span>
      </p>
      <nav class="wg-jump" aria-label="Jump to a Working Group">
        <a href="#wg1"><span class="wg-tag wg-1">WG1</span> Management & Coordination</a>
        <a href="#wg2"><span class="wg-tag wg-2">WG2</span> Framework Development</a>
        <a href="#wg3"><span class="wg-tag wg-3">WG3</span> Tools & Training</a>
        <a href="#wg4"><span class="wg-tag wg-4">WG4</span> Inclusion & Dissemination</a>
      </nav>
    </div>
  </section>
  <!-- four <section id="wg{1..4}"> blocks -->
</main>
```

### 2.2 Per-WG section spec

Each section is identical in shape, differing by WG number, colour accent, and the hand-authored name plus purpose. Leadership cards, member roster, and the count render at runtime, with a correct hand-authored fallback in the static HTML.

```html
<section id="wg1" class="wg-section" data-wg="1"
         style="--wg-accent:#0a84ff;--wg-accent-2:#5b8def">
  <div class="container reveal">
    <div class="wg-section-head">
      <span class="wg-tag wg-1">WG1</span>
      <h2 data-wg-name>Management & Coordination</h2>
      <p class="wg-stat" data-wg-count><span>5</span> members</p>
    </div>
    <p class="wg-purpose" data-wg-purpose>Strategic steering, governance, and coordination of the Action's scientific and administrative workstreams.</p>

    <h3 class="wg-subhead">Leadership</h3>
    <div class="mc-grid" data-wg-leadership="1">
      <!-- static fallback: lead + co-lead .mc-card[data-slug] cards -->
    </div>

    <h3 class="wg-subhead">Members</h3>
    <ul class="wg-members" data-wg-members="1" aria-label="WG1 members">
      <!-- static fallback roster of <li><a class="member-link" data-slug>…</a></li> -->
    </ul>

    <h3 class="wg-subhead">Related activities</h3>
    <ul class="wg-activities" data-wg-activities="1"><!-- §4 --></ul>
  </div>
</section>
```

Members render as a compact name list, not a card grid. The directory at `/people.html` stays the canonical card directory. The design target is roughly 145 cost.eu members, so four full popover-card grids would be heavy and would duplicate the directory. Each roster name is a popover trigger (see 2.3). The `data-wg-members` hook supports a `.mc-grid` swap if the maintainer later wants card parity, but the list is the recommendation.

### 2.3 Components reused, not reinvented

| Need | Reuse | Real anchor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fetch + locale + fail-soft render | `home-events.js` pattern (`pickLocale`, off-DOM fragment, `console.debug` on error) | `assets/js/home-events.js` |
| WG colours | `.wg-chip.wg-{1..4}` / `.wg-tag` plus an inline `--wg-accent` custom property | `assets/css/site.css:530-533`, `:483` |
| Leadership card photo + name hydration | the `.mc-card[data-slug]` binder | `assets/js/site.js:336` |
| Member popover on roster names | **see prerequisite below** | `essc-2026.html` (inline) |
| Freshness stamp | top-level `generated_at`, formatted exactly as on the directory | `people.html:1182` |

Prerequisite the adversarial reviews surfaced: there is no shared popover module. The popover is inlined in `essc-2026.html` and its FR/DE variants, and `site.js:336` only refreshes photo and name, it does not open a popover. So roster popover triggers are inert until one of two things ships:

- **Recommended for Phase 1:** make each roster `.member-link` a plain deep-link to `/people.html#<slug>`, which already auto-expands the matching directory card (task #57 / #121). No extraction dependency, lighter, and it routes the reader to the canonical directory.
- **Phase 2 option:** extract the ESSC inline popover to `assets/js/member-popover.js`, re-point all three ESSC locales at it, and load it on the WG page. Tracked as its own task with its own test (see phasing).

### 2.4 Nav, sitemap, SEO

- Repoint the `Working Groups` nav item from `index.html#working-groups` to `working-groups.html` across every locale nav block. The home `#working-groups` anchor still exists as a teaser target.
- `scripts/inject-seo.py:45` — add `"working-groups"` to the `PAGES` list, run it to regenerate canonical, Open Graph, hreflang, JSON-LD, and `sitemap.xml`.
- `sitemap.html` (plus FR and DE) — add a visual entry under *Working areas*.
- Footer link strip — optionally add *Working groups*.

### 2.5 Accessibility

`wg-jump` is a labelled `<nav>`. Each WG is a `<section>` whose first child is its `<h2>`, so the section is named without extra ARIA. Each `id` is a fragment skip target. Roster `<ul>`s carry `aria-label`. The sync cue and any pulse-dot are hidden in print. The palette already ships dark-mode-safe (WG4 carries dark text on amber); the `--wg-accent` tint must reuse the same hex tokens so dark-mode coverage is automatic.

### 2.6 FR and DE

`working-groups.fr.html` and `.de.html` are hand-translated (no machine translation, CLAUDE.md §1), carrying the `data-i18n-status="beta"` ribbon (*Traduction manuelle* / *Manuell übersetzt*). Because person names and leadership come from one locale-agnostic data layer, the three HTML files carry no person's name except as fallback, collapsing the roughly 72 leader-name copies the audit counted to zero in live markup. The translatable surface is the page chrome (head, lede, sync cue, subheads, role labels) plus the WG names and purposes. Where those WG names and purposes live (HTML vs JSON) is the open i18n decision in 5.2.

## 3. Zero-manual-maintenance data architecture (the headline)

### 3.1 The correction the whole design rests on

The cost-sync audit claims `wg_leadership` is synced. It is not. Verified in the live tree:

- `scripts/sync-cost.py:251` writes `"wg_leadership": {}` in the seed template and nothing else ever touches it.
- The eight populated `wg_leadership` values in today's `bios.json` are hand-seeded. On the next real cost.eu leadership change, `apply_leadership()` updates the flat `roles` string but leaves `wg_leadership` frozen, so any surface reading `wg_leadership` silently shows the old leader.

Task #207 (issue #236) is marked completed in this repo's history but did not close this derivation gap, so it is a reopen, not a fresh find. **The single build step that makes this entire design true is teaching `sync-cost.py` to derive `wg_leadership` and `wgs` from the `roles` strings.** Until it lands, the page is not self-updating.

Two more verified facts shape the sync code:

- Role spellings are mixed: WGs use `WG1 Co-Leader` (suffix `Leader`), the coordinator uses `Grant Awarding Coordinator Co-lead`. A regex anchored on `Co-Lead$` (as one proposal wrote) matches neither. The correct match is `^WG(\d) (Co-)?Leader$` for WG roles.
- `apply_leadership()` already reconciles roles on **every** entry, seed or form (commit a4c221d). The "extend to form entries" change one proposal asked for is already merged. Do not re-scope it.

### 3.2 New data file: `data/wg.json`

`wg.json` becomes the single rendered source for every WG and Action-leadership name on the site. Person names resolve to bios `id` slugs so renderers hydrate photo and affiliation from `bios.json` without duplicating them, and carry `display_name` so a fresh cost.eu leader with no bio yet still renders.

```json
{
  "_meta": {
    "source": "https://www.cost.eu/actions/CA24154/",
    "synced": "2026-05-26",
    "note": "Auto-written by scripts/sync-cost.py. Do not hand-edit synced fields. Only working_groups[].name + working_groups[].purpose are maintainer-owned."
  },
  "action_leadership": [
    { "role": "Action Chair",                     "slug": "moritz-weiss",    "display_name": "Dr Moritz Weiss" },
    { "role": "Action Vice-Chair",                 "slug": "marie-robin",     "display_name": "Dr Marie Robin" },
    { "role": "Science Communication Coordinator", "slug": "eugenio-sanchez", "display_name": "Mr Eugenio Sánchez" },
    { "role": "Grant Awarding Coordinator",        "slug": "eliza-gheorghe",  "display_name": "Dr Eliza Gheorghe",
      "co_lead": { "slug": "chiara-libiseller", "display_name": "Dr Chiara Libiseller" } }
  ],
  "working_groups": [
    {
      "number": 1,
      "colour": 1,
      "name":    { "en": "Management & Coordination", "fr": "Gestion et coordination", "de": "Management und Koordination" },
      "purpose": { "en": "Strategic steering, governance, and coordination of the Action's scientific and administrative workstreams.", "fr": "…", "de": "…" },
      "lead":    { "slug": "moritz-weiss", "display_name": "Dr Moritz Weiss" },
      "co_lead": { "slug": "filip-ejdus",  "display_name": "Prof Filip Ejdus" },
      "member_count": 38
    }
  ]
}
```

Field ownership, the point of the whole design:

| Field | Owner | Hand-edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action_leadership[]` role + slug + co-lead pairing | cost.eu via `extract_leadership` | never |
| `working_groups[].lead` / `co_lead` | cost.eu | never |
| `working_groups[].member_count` | counted from `WG_MAP` | never |
| `working_groups[].number` / `colour` | static 1 to 4 | once at file creation |
| `working_groups[].name` | maintainer | rarely (a WG rename) |
| `working_groups[].purpose` | maintainer, EN+FR+DE | the only routine hand-edit |
| `_meta.synced` | cost.eu sync date | never |

### 3.3 The `action_leadership` co-lead pairing (review fix)

The Action Leadership block on `about.html` is driven by `roles` strings, not `wg_leadership`. The coordinator and its co-lead are two separate `bios.json` entries linked only by the substring relationship `"Grant Awarding Coordinator"` inside `"Grant Awarding Coordinator Co-lead"`. The sync, not the renderer, resolves this pairing into the nested `co_lead` object shown above, so the renderer never has to string-match at runtime. Build `action_leadership` from an explicit allowlist of role labels, not a `Chair|Coordinator` substring match, because a naive `Coordinator` match wrongly pulls `Grant Awarding Coordinator Co-lead` in as a fifth officer:

```
ACTION_ROLES = ["Action Chair", "Action Vice-Chair",
                "Science Communication Coordinator",
                "Grant Awarding Coordinator",
                "Grant Holder Scientific Representative"]
```

For each allowlisted role `R`, the holder is the member whose `roles` contains `R`; the co-lead, if any, is the member whose `roles` contains `f"{R} Co-lead"`.

### 3.4 Exact `sync-cost.py` changes

1. **Derive `wg_leadership` in `apply_leadership()`.** In the existing all-entries reconciliation loop, after a role is kept, parse `^WG(\d) (Co-)?Leader$`: a bare `Leader` sets `wg_leadership.lead`, a `Co-Leader` sets `wg_leadership.co_lead`. Clear stale keys for WG roles no longer held. This is the blocking prerequisite (3.1).
2. **Union led and co-led WG numbers into `wgs[]`.** A leader is a member of the WG they lead. This fixes the verified integrity gap where Ruffa (WG3 lead), Kerschbaum (WG2 co-lead), and D'Amato (WG3 co-lead) all carry `wgs: []` and would otherwise appear in their WG's Leadership block but be absent from the Members list below it. Fixing the data benefits the directory too.
3. **Canonicalise the co-lead label.** Emit one consistent suffix so `bios.json` stops mixing `Co-Leader` (WGs) and `Co-lead` (coordinator). Pick one, document it in `docs/bios-setup.md`, test it.
4. **New `build_wg_json(leadership, new_map)`.** Reuses the `leadership` list and `new_map` already in memory at the foot of `main()`. Builds `action_leadership` via the 3.3 allowlist and pairing; builds `working_groups[].lead`/`co_lead` from the `WG(\d) (Co-)?Leader` tuples; sets `member_count = sum(1 for wgs in new_map.values() if n in wgs)`. **Carry-forward rule:** read any existing `wg.json` first and preserve `name`, `colour`, `purpose`, and `_meta.note`. Never overwrite a present maintainer field with an empty one. On a missing file, do not invent blank names; the file ships hand-seeded (see cold-start, 5.3).
5. **Date-churn guard.** Exclude `_meta.synced` from change detection. Bump it only when a synced field actually changed, otherwise the weekly no-op sync rewrites the file with a date-only diff and dirties the tree every Monday (CLAUDE.md §8). Mirror the existing `if diffs:` guard.
6. **Stamp `cost_synced_on`** into `bios.json` from `sync-cost.py`. Do not reuse `generated_at` or `meta.last_synced`, which are written by `sync-bios.py` (the form sync) and would mislabel a form-only refresh as a cost.eu sync. The public freshness cue can read either `wg.json._meta.synced` or this field.
7. **Wire into `main()`** with one `build_wg_json(...)` call and print its diff lines.
8. **Tests** in `scripts/test-sync-cost.py`, mirroring `test_extract_leadership_*`: `test_wg_leadership_derived` (fixture `WG1 Co-Leader` to `{co_lead:[1]}`), `test_leader_unioned_into_wgs`, `test_build_wg_json_pairs_action_co_lead`, `test_build_wg_json_preserves_purpose`, `test_build_wg_json_missing_file_does_not_blank_names`.

### 3.5 Renderers and surfaces converted from hand-coded to data-driven

| Surface | Today | After | Drives from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `working-groups.html` (new) | does not exist | render leadership + roster + count + purpose | `wg.json` + `bios.json` |
| Home `#working-groups` (`index.html:356-402`) | hand-coded names **and** purpose prose, **no data hooks** | add `data-wg="N"` to each `<article>` plus `data-wg-name`/`data-wg-purpose`/lead/co-lead hooks, then render | `wg.json` |
| About *Action Leadership* (`about.html:451-479`) | hand-coded, `data-slug` present | render from `action_leadership[]` incl. co-lead pairing | `wg.json` + `bios.json` |
| About *WG Leadership* + *Co-Leaders* (`about.html:481-541`) | hand-coded across 3 locales | collapse the two grids into one (each WG card shows lead + co-lead), render | `wg.json` |
| Directory WG pills (`people.html`) | already data-driven | unchanged, now also benefits from `wgs[]` union | `bios.json` |

Retired hand-coded duplicates, explicitly:

- The eight WG lead/co-lead names hand-typed in `index.html` and `about.html` across three locales (the audit's ~72 copies).
- The four WG names duplicated between `index.html` `<h3>`s and `about.html` role labels, now single-sourced in `wg.json`.
- The four WG purpose sentences on the home cards, now single-sourced in `wg.json.purpose` and read by both the home cards and the WG page (this is the half of the GOAL one proposal under-counted; it ships in the same PR, not a follow-up).
- The five-card *Working Group Co-Leaders* grid on About, folded into the WG Leadership grid.

What stays hand-coded as fail-soft fallback only: the existing static HTML in each surface. The reviews flag a real risk here: the fallback is the very drift being eliminated, so a fetch failure resurrects whatever the static markup says. Therefore at cutover, reconcile each surface's static lead/co-lead against `bios.json` first, so the fallback degrades to correct data, then wire the renderer. This is an explicit cutover step, not an afterthought.

### 3.6 How leadership flows from cost.eu, and the lag

A single cost.eu leadership change now produces a one-line `bios.json` diff (plus a `wg.json` diff) that drives five surfaces at once. That is the win and it concentrates, rather than increases, the review burden. Make the cost-sync PR body render-aware: alongside the existing `report_wg()` diff, print a "Surfaces affected" line and an orphan detector (5.1) at the top.

The 3 to 4 day lag is surfaced, not hidden. Every WG and leadership surface shows a quiet `Updated <date>` cue reading the sync date, modelled on the ESSC pulsing-dot liveness marker (show-don't-tell, CLAUDE.md §6), never a paragraph explaining the pipeline. The worst-case path (cost.eu publishes after 3 to 4 days, then the Monday 05:00 sync runs) is roughly ten days; a manual workflow dispatch cuts it to about four. We reject a manual-override field: it reintroduces the exact hand-edited duplicate this design deletes and creates an expiry/contradiction problem. The override is the existing manual dispatch, and a genuinely urgent public announcement uses the What's New banner (CLAUDE.md §14).

## 4. Activities, events tagging, and directory tie-ins

### 4.1 Event-to-WG tagging (one optional field, degrades to nothing)

Add two optional fields to each object in `data/events.json`, alongside `eventType` and `featured`:

- `wg` — array of WG integers an event is specifically tied to, e.g. `[1, 3]`. Strictly numeric so it shares one type with the directory filter (`wgs.includes(Number(...))` at `people.html:666`).
- `wgScope` — `"cross"` for events that span all WGs by design (the Summer School, ESSC), or absent/`"specific"`.

One shared resolver: `eventWGs(ev)` returns `[1,2,3,4]` for `cross`, else `ev.wg || []`. The WG page's activities strip for `#wgN` filters `events.filter(ev => eventWGs(ev).includes(N))`, sorted by `start`. Empty sections render nothing (no placeholder copy to translate). These tags are editorial judgement, not cost.eu data (cost.eu has no event taxonomy), so this overlay does not touch the prime sync story.

### 4.2 WG chip on event cards (home grid)

In `home-events.js`, render a WG chip cluster in the existing pill row, reusing `.wg-chip.wg-{1..4}` (zero new colour CSS). A `cross` event shows a single neutral "All WGs" chip (one new rule, `.event-wg-chip--all`); specific events show coloured chips that deep-link to `working-groups.html#wgN`. ESSC sessions are not individually WG-tagged in this iteration; that is a separate change against the Indico session model, tracked as a follow-up.

### 4.3 Directory deep-link (reuse the existing hash grammar)

The directory filter already parses `#keywords=a,b` via `URLSearchParams`, disambiguating structured filters from bare member slugs by the presence of `=` (`people.html:1019-1028`). Extend the same grammar with `wg`: each WG section links "See all WG2 members in the directory" to `people.html#wg=2`. Add an `applyHashWG()` mirroring `parseHashKeywords()`, called on load and from the existing `hashchange` handler before `render()`, setting `activeWG` and the chips' `aria-pressed`. `#wg=2&keywords=cyber-defence` composes for free because both read one `URLSearchParams`. Keeping WG selection in the hash preserves the directory's one disambiguation rule.

### 4.4 Future datasets

STSMs and outputs, when their JSON files land, get the same optional `wg` + `wgScope` pair and a second filtered strip on each WG section via a generalised `recordWGs(record)`. Do not build placeholder strips for datasets that do not exist; add the strip in the PR that adds the dataset. Track as a milestoned follow-up.

## 5. Edge cases, i18n, and maintenance

### 5.1 Failure modes and mitigations

- **Name spelling changes on cost.eu break `norm()` matching.** A rename produces a new `WG_MAP` key; `apply_wgs_to_bios()` finds no matching bio and leaves that bio's `wgs` untouched, so the bio silently keeps stale WGs. Mitigation: an orphan detector in the sync PR body listing every non-seed `bios.json` member whose `norm(name)` is absent from `new_map`, and every `WG_MAP` key with no matching bio, under "Unmatched after sync — possible name change or departure." Important correction from the reviews: adding a `name_aliases` entry fixes only the popover and directory display. `apply_wgs_to_bios()` matches on the bio's own `name` field, so the maintainer must also update that `name` (or `apply_wgs_to_bios` must be taught to try `name_aliases`) for the WG membership to re-sync. State which path is used.
- **A leader steps down (the lag).** During the gap the page shows the departed leader. The freshness cue carries the "as of" date. An absent `co_lead` for a WG renders "Co-lead: vacant", so an empty seat is visible rather than silently dropped.
- **A member in zero WGs, or in all four.** Leadership placement is driven by `wg_leadership`, membership by `wgs`; they are independent. A zero-WG non-leader (e.g. the Grant Awarding Coordinator) does not appear in any WG section but does appear in the Action Leadership block. A member in all four recurs in all four sections, which is correct.
- **A leader or member with no bio or no photo.** Degrade per-field, never crash a card: no photo falls back to the existing initials/placeholder; a name present only in `WG_MAP` with no bio renders as a plain name (counts toward the total, no dead "View full profile"); a seed leader renders name + role + placeholder. Name-only entries are the visible nudge that someone has not filled the directory form, surfaced to the maintainer via the orphan detector. We do not auto-create bio skeletons for plain members (only for office holders, as today), to avoid flooding the directory with empty cards.

### 5.2 i18n

| Content | Source | Locale handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WG names, purposes | `wg.json` (or HTML, see decision) | hand-translated EN+FR+DE |
| Person names | `bios.json` | locale-neutral, never translated |
| Role labels, "Lead", "Co-lead", "vacant", the sync cue, subheads | page chrome | hand-translated short static strings |
| WG membership, counts | `bios.json` + `WG_MAP` | locale-neutral, derived |

The drift checker (`scripts/check-i18n-drift.py`) hashes the EN **HTML** source. If WG purposes live in `wg.json`, an EN purpose edit does not change the HTML hash, so FR/DE will not flag stale. This is a real hole. Two honest options, and the maintainer chooses (6, decision 2):

- **(a)** keep purposes in `wg.json` and extend the drift checker to hash the EN JSON strings. Preserves one render path; costs a new JSON-keyed tracking mechanism in the checker (more than the "20 lines" one proposal claimed).
- **(b)** keep WG names and purposes as short static `data-i18n` blocks in the HTML, and let `wg.json` hold only `{number, colour, lead, co_lead, member_count}` plus the `action_leadership`. The existing file-SHA drift checker then works with zero new code, at the cost of the four short paragraphs living in three HTML files.

Recommendation: **(b)** for the descriptions specifically. It keeps the drift checker honest with no new machinery, and four short paragraphs in three files is a small, bounded duplication that the checker actively polices. `wg.json` still single-sources all the synced leadership data, which is where the maintenance pain actually was.

Register `working-groups.html` in `data/i18n-state.json` and `check-i18n-drift.py` after the FR/DE variants exist, and `--mark-fresh` to seed.

### 5.3 Cold start

Ship the initial `data/wg.json` hand-authored with the four numbers, colours, names, and EN+FR+DE purposes (if option 5.2a) in the same PR that adds `build_wg_json`. The sync's carry-forward rule must treat a missing or absent maintainer field as "leave it", never "write empty", and the missing-file path is unit-tested so a fresh run cannot blank the names.

### 5.4 Voice

New prose follows CLAUDE.md §6 and §7: British English, no "source of truth" (say "the COST directory" or "cost.eu" and reuse one referent), no em dashes, no prose semicolons, no rule-of-three padding. The existing home-page purpose sentences already comply and seed the EN copy verbatim.

## 6. Phasing

**Phase 1 — the sync truth (blocking, the real unlock).** Effort: medium. `sync-cost.py` derives `wg_leadership` and unions led WGs into `wgs[]`, canonicalises the co-lead label, builds `data/wg.json` (with the action co-lead pairing, carry-forward, and date-churn guard), stamps `cost_synced_on`, and prints the orphan detector plus "surfaces affected" in the PR body. Tests added. Ship the hand-seeded `wg.json`. No visible site change yet; this is the foundation, and without it nothing else is self-updating.

**Phase 2 — render the new page and convert surfaces.** Effort: medium to large. Build `working-groups.html` + FR + DE and `assets/js/wg-render.js`; convert the home `#working-groups` cards (add `data-wg` hooks first) and the About leadership grids to render-from-JSON, reconciling each static fallback against `bios.json` at cutover; roster names deep-link to `/people.html#<slug>` (popover extraction deferred). Register in `inject-seo.py`, `sitemap.html`, the drift checker. Repoint nav. This is the duplicate-elimination PR.

**Phase 3 — activities, tagging, popover extraction.** Effort: small to medium. Add `wg`/`wgScope` to `events.json` and the home-card WG chips; add `applyHashWG()` to the directory; add the per-WG activities strip; optionally extract the shared member-popover module and give the roster real popovers. Each piece is independently shippable.

The one content cost across all phases: four short WG descriptions, hand-authored in EN and hand-translated to FR and DE, authored once and edited only on a WG rename or re-scope. Everything else flows from cost.eu.

## 7. Open decisions for the maintainer

1. **Roster popover vs deep-link.** Phase 1 ships roster names as `/people.html#<slug>` deep-links (no extraction dependency). Approve, or commit to extracting the shared popover module in Phase 2 so WG-page names open a popover in place.
2. **Where WG descriptions live (5.2).** Option (a) `wg.json` + extend the drift checker, or recommended option (b) short `data-i18n` HTML blocks + zero checker change. This decides how much new i18n machinery ships.
3. **Members as a list or a card grid (2.2).** Recommendation is a compact roster, keeping `/people.html` canonical. Confirm, or opt for `.mc-grid` card parity per section.
4. **About *Action Leadership* block.** Render it from `action_leadership[]` in this work (recommended, closes the third of the three named change types), or accept it stays hand-coded and document that an Action-Chair change still needs a manual About edit.
5. **Co-lead canonical label (3.4 step 3).** Pick the one spelling the sync emits site-wide (`Co-Lead` / `Co-lead` / `Co-Leader`); it becomes the documented convention.
6. **Reopen issue #236 / task #207.** The `wg_leadership` derivation was in that issue's scope but did not land, so Phase 1 reopens it rather than filing fresh. Confirm the reopen and milestone (CLAUDE.md §3, §10).
